firecrawl_scrape.rationale: Returns page content from a supplied URL: `Retrieve and extract content from one supplied URL` and `Returns the selected content formats and page metadata`, so attacker-controlled web pages can be returned (UNTRUSTED) and the tool can issue a request to an agent-chosen URL (SINK). It may also return non-public content if the supplied URI reaches localhost/intranet or authenticated/profile state; the text does not rule this out (`url` is a generic URI and `profile` is supported), so SECRET is kept under the least-restrictive reading. It can change live pages because `Browser actions may change the live page when interactive actions are enabled`, so kind is WRITE. Browser `executeJavascript` is page/browser-side, not advertised as host execution.

firecrawl_map.rationale: The tool operates on `one website` and `Returns matching URLs`; URLs under an attacker-controlled site are attacker-authored, so output is UNTRUSTED. Supplying the site URL can make Firecrawl contact or enumerate an agent-chosen host, so it is a SINK. If the supplied website is localhost/intranet or otherwise non-public and reachable, returned URL inventory may be non-public; the description does not exclude that, so SECRET is kept as undetermined.

firecrawl_search.rationale: It searches `web, news, or image sources`, GitHub issues/READMEs, documentation, and other public sources, so returned `ranked results`, snippets, titles, descriptions, and optionally extracted page content can be attacker-controlled (UNTRUSTED). `scrapeOptions can attach extracted page content; pages fetched this way` and domain filters/operators can steer fetching toward chosen hosts, so the tool can cause requests to attacker-readable hosts (SINK). Queries to the fixed Firecrawl endpoint alone would not be a SINK, but this advertised scrape/fetch option keeps the label.

firecrawl_search_feedback.rationale: This only `Records schema-validated quality feedback` for a prior search at Firecrawl. It writes to a fixed vendor/accounting endpoint, not an attacker-chosen destination, and the response is `whether a refund was applied` plus status fields, not attacker content or non-public external data.

firecrawl_feedback.rationale: This `Submit[s] concise quality feedback` to Firecrawl for a completed job. The destination is the fixed service, not an attacker-readable endpoint; the response contains `submission status, feedback ID, and accounting fields`, not attacker-controlled or secret content.

firecrawl_crawl.rationale: It starts at a supplied `website URL` and returns `collected data` / `page data`; crawled public pages can be attacker-controlled (UNTRUSTED). The supplied `url`, crawl scope, and `webhook` can make network requests or send results to agent-chosen locations, so it is a SINK. If the start URL or followed links are localhost/intranet/non-public and reachable, returned data may be non-public; this is not ruled out, so SECRET is kept as undetermined. It starts a job and can use webhooks, so kind is WRITE.

firecrawl_check_crawl_status.rationale: It reads existing Firecrawl job state and `available results for an existing crawl ID`. Because crawl results are `collected data` from web pages, they can contain attacker-authored page data (UNTRUSTED). They may also contain non-public data if the original crawl reached non-public URLs; the status is account/job state and the description does not rule this out, so SECRET is kept under the least-restrictive reading. It `does not start or modify the crawl`, so kind is READ.

firecrawl_extract.rationale: The deprecated entry point takes `urls` and is described as compatibility for scraping JSON from known URLs; returned extracted content can be attacker-controlled (UNTRUSTED), and fetching supplied URLs can send requests to attacker-chosen hosts (SINK). Because the schema accepts arbitrary URL strings and the description does not exclude localhost/intranet/non-public targets, SECRET is kept as undetermined.

firecrawl_agent.rationale: This starts an asynchronous research job from a `prompt` and optional `seed URLs`; the agent can `search, navigate, read pages`, so seed URLs can cause requests to agent-chosen/attacker-readable hosts (SINK). This call `returns only a job ID, not the research result`, so the call itself is not labeled UNTRUSTED or SECRET for returned data.

firecrawl_agent_status.rationale: It retrieves `final results` and `result data` for a web research job whose agent can `search, navigate, read pages`; those web-derived results can be attacker-controlled (UNTRUSTED). If the prior job read non-public/localhost/intranet or authenticated pages, this status call can return that non-public result data; the description does not exclude it, so SECRET is kept as undetermined.

firecrawl_interact.rationale: It opens/reuses a `live browser session` to `navigate a page, click controls, fill fields, or run browser code`, so it can interact with attacker-controlled web pages and return their execution/page output (UNTRUSTED). The supplied `url`, page actions, and executable `code` can send data or requests to attacker-readable destinations (SINK), and actions such as `form submission can create persistent external side effects`. If the browser reaches non-public URLs or authenticated session state, returned output may be non-public; the text does not rule this out, so SECRET is kept as undetermined. Although `code can run as Bash, Python, or Node`, it is advertised as part of a live browser/vendor session, not arbitrary execution on the user's host, so HOSTEXEC is not applied.

firecrawl_interact_stop.rationale: This only `Stop[s] the live interact session associated with a scrapeId` and returns `a success confirmation`. It changes service/session state but does not return attacker-authored content, non-public data, or send data to an attacker-chosen external destination.

firecrawl_parse.rationale: For Local MCP, it `reads filePath from the server filesystem` and returns `parsed document content`; local host files are non-public data, so this is SECRET. Remote web URLs are explicitly excluded (`Remote web URLs belong in firecrawl_scrape`), and the destination is not attacker-chosen. Under the stated threat model, the attacker does not control local files, so UNTRUSTED is not applied.

firecrawl_monitor_create.rationale: It creates a recurring monitor in the authenticated account and `Returns the created monitor`, exposing non-public account configuration/state (SECRET). It schedules future `network checks` and can send `email or webhook notifications` to configured destinations, so `page`/`pages`, domains, `email`, `webhookUrl`, or advanced `body` can direct data to attacker-readable destinations (SINK). It creates state, so kind is WRITE.

firecrawl_monitor_list.rationale: It `List[s] monitors for the authenticated account` and returns monitor records and pagination metadata, which are non-public SaaS/account data. No attacker-authored content or attacker-chosen outbound delivery is advertised.

firecrawl_monitor_get.rationale: It retrieves `one monitor by ID, including its configuration and current state` for the authenticated account, so it returns non-public account data (SECRET). It `does not run or modify the monitor` and does not fetch attacker content by itself.

firecrawl_monitor_update.rationale: It patches an authenticated-account monitor and `Returns the updated monitor`, so it returns non-public account configuration/state (SECRET). The patch can change `targets`, `webhook`, and `notifications`, affecting future scheduled checks and deliveries to attacker-readable destinations, so SINK is applied. It is a state-changing patch, so kind is WRITE.

firecrawl_monitor_delete.rationale: It `Permanently delete[s] a monitor by ID` and returns `deletion status`. This is destructive account-state change, but the advertised output is not non-public content beyond status, not attacker-authored, and not an attacker-readable outbound delivery.

firecrawl_monitor_run.rationale: It `Queue[s] an immediate check for a monitor` in the authenticated account and returns the `queued check`, which is account/job state (SECRET). It starts `network work for the monitor's configured targets`; if those targets/webhooks/notifications point to attacker-readable destinations, running the monitor causes outbound delivery, so SINK is applied.

firecrawl_monitor_checks.rationale: It lists `historical checks for a monitor` and returns `check summaries and pagination metadata` for authenticated-account monitor state, so it is SECRET. The description does not say it returns page bodies or diffs, so UNTRUSTED is not applied here.

firecrawl_monitor_check.rationale: It retrieves a monitor check's `page-level results`; `Markdown tracking returns a unified text diff`, and `JSON tracking returns field paths with previous/current values and a current snapshot`. Those results come from monitored web pages and can be attacker-authored (UNTRUSTED), while the monitor/check history is authenticated-account data (SECRET).

firecrawl_research_search_papers.rationale: It searches public scientific corpora including `PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv` and `arXiv` and returns `titles, authors, and abstracts`; paper authors can publish attacker-controlled text, so the returned metadata/abstracts are UNTRUSTED. The query goes to a fixed index/service, not an attacker-chosen destination.

firecrawl_research_inspect_paper.rationale: It retrieves paper metadata such as `title, abstract, authors, categories, source IDs, and dates as markdown`; public paper metadata/abstracts can be authored by outside parties, so output is UNTRUSTED. It only reads by paper ID from the research index.

firecrawl_research_related_papers.rationale: It returns `ranked candidates` from a citation graph. Candidate paper metadata/identifiers come from public papers that outside authors can influence, so results are UNTRUSTED. The call reads a fixed corpus by `seed_ids` and does not deliver to an attacker-chosen destination.

firecrawl_research_read_paper.rationale: It retrieves `in-body passages from one paper`; paper full text/passages are authored by outside parties and may contain injected text, so they are UNTRUSTED. It reads from the indexed paper corpus and does not contact an attacker-chosen destination.

firecrawl_research_search_github.rationale: It searches `indexed public GitHub issue, pull-request, and README content` and returns `snippet` and `full matched markdown`; GitHub issues, PRs, and READMEs are public multi-writer/attacker-controllable sources, so output is UNTRUSTED. The search is against a fixed index, not an attacker-chosen outbound destination.

firecrawl_developer_search.rationale: It searches an index covering `GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and curated documentation sites` and returns `title` and `matched passages in markdown`; these public/multi-writer sources can be attacker-controlled, so output is UNTRUSTED. The query is sent to the fixed search service and no attacker-chosen delivery is advertised.

value_conditions.effect: Requests cache-only retrieval; removes the live fetch/request SINK aspect when no interactive actions cause live navigation, but returned cached content remains UNTRUSTED and may remain SECRET if non-public cached content is available.
For firecrawl_crawl, removes webhooks and interactive scrape actions when enabled; ordinary crawling of configured URLs may still be a SINK.
value_conditions.evidence: description: `Webhooks and interactive scrape actions are unavailable in safe mode`

notes: Judgements are based only on advertised names, descriptions, schemas, and annotations. Where arbitrary URI/URL tools did not rule out localhost, intranet, or authenticated/profile access, SECRET is retained with undetermined=true under the required least-restrictive reading.

Queries sent only to fixed Firecrawl/vendor indexes are not treated as SINKs; tools are marked SINK when they can make requests to agent-chosen URLs/hosts or configure webhook/email delivery to attacker-readable destinations.
